problem:
Consider the line $-4x+y+1=0$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=6.$

Consider the line $x=-2$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=14.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $x=-2$ passes through the points $G(-2,0)$ and $H(-2,1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $G$ and $H$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ -6 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${G}^{′}(2,-6)$ and ${H}^{′}(6,-4).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-6) & =\frac{-4-(-6)}{6-2}(x-2) \\ y+6 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+6 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-2) \\ 2y+12 & =x-2 \\ 12+2 & =x-2y \\ x-2y & =14\end{aligned}
$$
